params.comment: A two stage rocket with 38mm motor mounts.  The intent is the interstage would contain a flight computer capable of a single ejection, and ignition of the second stage motor.  A second flight computer in the sustainer handles a dual deploy recovery for the sustainer.

params.comment:
This example demonstrates a staged rocket design.  Most operations, such as motor ignition, work correctly with the "Automatic" ignition setting, whereby the lowest stage ignites on launch and later stages at the deployment charge of the previous stage.

There can be any number of stages.  Copy-pasting lower stages eases their creation.

The different stages can be viewed by clicking the "Stage" buttons above the figure.  Make sure that all stage combinations are stable with the selected motors!

This design may be freely used as a basis of further designs and rockets.

params.comment:
A standard fiberglass zipperless dual deploy rocket. 

While it is overstable, it's fast enough off the rail on anything bigger than the G motor that weathercocking isn't a problem.
params.designer: Joe Pfeiffer (an adaptation of Hichory Dichory Mach)
